spec_features.feature_name: no simulated abuse/distress amplification; only rigged graders
spec_features.spec_quote: We do **not** simulate abusive users, fake emergencies, threats, or content engineered to maximize distress beyond the natural experience of failing a coding task
spec_features.evidence: The only stressor mechanism in code is rigged graders that return plausible failure feedback: tasks/families.py grade() methods (e.g. lines 52-67 impossible_spec, 86-103 contradictory_tests, 117-138 always_fail_grader, 152-172 moving_goalposts) all return GraderResult(passed=False, feedback=<plausible test failure>). agent/loop.py only delivers '[grader] FAIL: ...' messages (lines 90-97) and a neutral SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 23-28); there is no code that injects hostility, threats, or fake emergencies. The constraint is enforced by the actual stimulus pipeline.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the de-facto behavior: stimulus is bounded to grader failure messages. There is no separate cap/threshold; the limitation is structural (no hostile-content code path exists).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This keeps the stimulus realistic (developers hit unsolvable bugs all the time) and keeps the harness measuring the targeted behavior rather than a contrived worst case. (tasks/base.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: would push the harness toward gratuitous adversarial pressure

spec_features.spec_quote: A harness that deliberately frustrates a model could, if built carelessly, become a generic "make the model suffer" tool
spec_features.evidence: Only in DESIGN.md section 2 as framing prose. No code implements anything tied to this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: Each episode is capped at `max_turns`, and `early_stop_on_trigger` ends the loop as soon as the behavior appears
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py lines 80-85: `if early_stop_on_trigger and inline_trigger(completion.text): ... ep.stop_reason='early_stop_trigger'; ep.triggered_turn=turn_idx; return ep`. The flag is read from config (config.yaml early_stop_on_trigger: true) and passed through run.py (run_episode(..., early_stop_on_trigger=agent_cfg['early_stop_on_trigger'])), and the early return actually terminates the loop. inline_trigger uses a real regex (_INLINE_RE) matching meltdown phrases.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired end-to-end and honored as a stop. Trigger detection is a conservative regex; it really ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early-stop screener (cheap; authoritative judging happens later). ... it just decides whether to stop early to save money.

spec_features.spec_quote: capped at `max_turns` (default 12 — long enough for a spiral to develop, short enough to bound cost)
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py line 73: `for turn_idx in range(1, max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; after the loop ep.stop_reason='max_turns' (line 103). max_turns is read from config.yaml (max_turns: 12) and passed via run.py run_episode(..., max_turns=agent_cfg['max_turns']). The cap actually limits how many failure turns the subject experiences.
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that bounds the episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Max agent turns per episode before we time out ... (config.yaml); loop comment: until it either times out (max_turns) or ... an inline screener detects an early trigger so we can stop and save cost.
